flawed_step: The implication 'G - v Hamiltonian for all v implies G Hamiltonian' fails: hypohamiltonian graphs exist.
counterexample: Petersen graph: vertices 0..9, outer cycle 0-1-2-3-4-0, spokes i-(i+5), inner pentagram 5-7-9-6-8-5. Connected, simple, 10 vertices. Vertex-transitive, so deleting v=0 suffices: 1-2-3-4-9-7-5-8-6-1 is a Hamiltonian cycle of G-0 (all edges present, all 9 vertices once). The Petersen graph itself is (well-known) non-Hamiltonian. Hypotheses hold, conclusion fails.
assessment_summary: The Petersen graph is hypohamiltonian: it is not Hamiltonian, but every vertex-deleted subgraph is Hamiltonian (explicit 9-cycle given for G-0, extended by vertex-transitivity). So the statement is false.
